# Goban Studio v6.0.0

v6 is about clarity and depth: a calmer interface, one report for every
game, a strength estimate you can trust more, an advanced course, an
opening explorer, and a board you can play by ear.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation. v5 can update itself to v6 from
Settings → About.

## A calmer interface

- **Review in three tabs**: the balance chart stays on top; *Analysis*
  (key mistakes and variations), *Summary* (the game in three phases — only
  when KataGo analysed the game) and *Notes* (comments, marks, the
  variation tree) below it.
- **Records open where it matters**: a game from your library opens on its
  final position and moves to the first key moment once the analysis is
  done; the Ear-Reddening Game opens on move 127, AlphaGo – Lee Sedol game
  4 on move 78.
- **Settings as a window with panes**: General, Board, Playing, Opponents
  and analysis, Data, About.
- Quiet empty states (an empty week is one line), the main keys in an empty
  move list, problem windows that keep stones at a natural size.

## A report for every game

- After a rated game, *See the report*: the result, the three phases
  (points lost, mistakes, blunders, accuracy), three key moments as small
  boards that open the review at that move, and *Practise this game*, which
  turns your worst mistakes into drills for the Daily five.
- *Export image* saves the report as a PNG. Reports are kept with the game;
  Library → a game's menu → Game report.
- With only the offline estimate, the report shows turning points and says
  plainly that it cannot tell how many points each phase cost.

## Learning

- **An advanced course** for about 5 kyu to 1 dan: 5 units and 15 lessons
  — whole-board judgement, invasion and reduction, advanced life and death
  (dead, ko or alive; ko; seki in the corner), combined tesuji (throw-in and
  snapback, connect-and-die, under the stones) and middle-game strategy.
  Players around 5 kyu who have finished the intermediate course go there
  next.
- **Endgame problems**: 34 new problems (find the biggest move, or how many
  points a move is worth), every answer proved by a new exact counting mode
  in the solver. 543 problems in all.
- **Leaning attack and sabaki**, the two intermediate lessons that were
  missing in v5. The course now has 18 units and 82 lessons.

## Opening explorer

- Library → Explorer: whole-board openings (star points, 3-4 points,
  sanrensei, Chinese, …) and corner joseki (star-point approaches, the 3-3
  invasion, 3-4 approaches), about 1,400 positions evaluated by KataGo and
  shipped with the app — it works offline.
- Every continuation is marked standard, playable or a mistake with its
  point loss; past the book the desktop app continues with live analysis.
  *Play from here* starts a game from the position. Review notes where a
  19×19 game left the book.

## Accessibility

- With a screen reader the board can be played without sight: moves,
  captures, passes and results are spoken; arrow keys read the point; keys
  read a group and its liberties, the last move, whose turn, captures, a
  row, a column or the whole board. Review, problems and lessons speak too.
- Every control can be reached by keyboard, with a visible focus ring;
  segmented controls take the arrow keys. *Larger text* in Settings →
  General (⌘= / ⌘−).

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test, a strong player's review of
  the advanced course, the endgame problems and the explorer's names, a
  native-speaker review of the Chinese, Korean and Japanese text, and the
  board with a real VoiceOver, Narrator or NVDA session (the spoken text is
  tested, not the screen readers).
- The opening book was made with the standard network at 250 visits per
  position; values are good for comparing moves, not exact. Kobayashi and
  mini-Chinese lines are not in it yet.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.
- Some shapes in the advanced course are taught without their traditional
  name (the L group, the carpenter's square) because the diagram could not
  be confirmed.

## Your data

Everything from v5 carries over.
